port_provenance.reason: Preserves donor BCT channel-axis normalization, affine transform, fused ReLU, and complete input/weight/bias adjoints. OARS assigns crate-global IDs because donor-local 326 through 329 already identify the scaled masked-softmax and attention family, makes the donor shader's four-values-per-lane limit an explicit 1024-channel contract, and uses the schema-owned ordered sum-axis reducer for affine adjoints.

Preserves donor norm-before-gate RMS normalization, cyclic broadcast affine groups, optional bias, SiLU gate, complete input/gate/affine adjoints, and ordered affine reduction. Rust exposes optional bias explicitly and reuses the existing schema-owned sum-axis reducer.

Preserves the donor fused projection split, per-group B/C RMS normalization, clamped softplus dt, heavy-tail A-times-dt transform, eight-output semantic boundary, and fused reverse formula. Rust assigns crate-global IDs because donor-local ID 204 already names the Cryptography Merkle copy, replaces the donor contended floating-point atomic with an ordered second-stage dt-bias reduction, and represents all output adjoints with one tape node.

Preserves the donor FP32 SISO selective recurrence, grouped Q/K sharing, rotary cumulative angle, trapezoidal gate coupling, optional z and D paths, deterministic short-sequence reverse stages, bounded generic chunk-recompute reverse, exact eleven-input/eleven-adjoint semantic boundary, and four-buffer recurrent step state. Rust models each mutated recurrent buffer as an explicit semantic alias output so graph state advances in SSA order; one deterministic lowering-only reduction replaces the donor's nested general-purpose semantic reductions.

Preserves the donor shared-state MIMO rank expansion and contraction, optional rankwise gate and output normalization, deterministic complete adjoint, grouped Q/K reduction, and four-buffer recurrent step.
